title: Granular Reserve Lifecycle and Autotune for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD for a granular reservation lifecycle and autotune recommendations engine for Dedicated capacity. Introduces time-windowed reservation slices (reserve windows), an autotuner that suggests reserve sizes/headroom based on observed traffic, and explicit burst token accounting with controlled preemption tiers. Goals: reduce wasted reserved capacity, improve burst availability for paying tenants, and keep latency SLOs stable under transient surges while maintaining strong isolation guarantees.
problem_statement: Customers with reserved GPU capacity either overprovision to avoid tail latency in surges or underprovision and rely on brittle burst heuristics. Current reserved pools are static, leading to wasted spend or SLO violations during unpredictable traffic patterns. There's no system-level autotuning to recommend reservation sizes or headroom for Dedicated customers, and burst handling lacks transparent token accounting and operator-runbooks.
goals: Enable time-windowed reservation slices (reserve windows) that let tenants reserve capacity for specific recurrence patterns and temporary spikes
Provide an autotune recommendations engine that suggests reserved capacity and headroom targets based on 90/95/99th percentile consumption and growth trends
Implement burst token accounting with explicit budgets, preemption tiers, and transparent fallbacks to lower-cost model variants
Expose tenant QoS class and isolation controls that map to capacity preemption and eviction policies
Ship operator dashboards and an on-call playbook for burst incidents
non_goals: Replace Dedicated global autoscaler implementation (this is complementary, not a rework)
Implement model-level quantization/autotune recommendations (out of scope for this PRD)
Support cross-region reserve pooling in phase 1
user_stories: As a platform engineer, I want the system to suggest a reserve window and headroom for my tenant based on last 30 days traffic so I can set a cost-efficient contract
As an SRE, I want burst tokens surfaced in the Console and alerts when token burn rate exceeds predictions so I can intervene before SLO violations
As a product owner, I want tenants to be assigned explicit isolation classes so we can define graceful degradation policies tied to paid tiers
As an operator, I want a clear rollback and preemption log for any eviction so we can audit incidents
requirements: Reserve windows: create, edit, and remove time-windowed reservations (cron-like recurrence + one-off windows)
Autotune engine: ingest per-tenant tokenized usage, compute suggested reserve and headroom with configurable safety multiplier, output recommended reserve change and expected cost delta
Burst tokens: allocate a burn-rate budget per tenant, persist ledger of token burns, enforce emergency cutoff when safety budget exhausted
Preemption tiers: define at least three tiers (SLA-priority, best-effort-warm, preemptible) and mapping rules from tenant QoS classes
Operator UX: Console panel listing reserve windows, token budgets, suggested autotune changes, and one-click accept/decline for recommendations
API: endpoints to query, accept, update reserve windows and token budgets; audit log entries for changes

SLO integration: autoscale/autotune must respect model-specific latency SLOs (configurable per tenant) and never recommend reserve shrinkage that increases 99th latency beyond the configured threshold
Telemetry: emit metrics for reserved utilization, wasted-reserve percentage, burst-token-burn-rate, suggested vs applied recommendations
Security: all API operations require tenant-scoped auth; changes generate immutable audit entries; security review required for autotune model inputs
acceptance_criteria: Autotune engine runs in a sandbox and produces suggestions for at least 90% of tenants with >72 hours of telemetry
Suggested reserve changes include an explicit expected delta in monthly cost and projected SLO impact
Console surfaces reserve windows and allows operator to accept/decline a recommendation; accepting triggers an API event and an audit log entry
Burst token ledger persists burns and can be queried via API within 200ms p95
When burst token budgets are exhausted, lower preemption tiers are used and higher-tier tenants are not affected (manual test against synthetic workload)
End-to-end tests prove that a tenant with recommended reserve applied shows a >=15% reduction in wasted-reserve metric across a rolling 14-day window in staging
Security review completed and signed-off by security team prior to canary rollout
scope_changes: Phase 1: UI + API + sandboxed autotune recommendations only (no automatic apply)
Phase 2: opt-in automatic apply for vetted tenants after safety window and rollback hooks are in place
Removed: cross-region aggregated reserves for phase 1; to be revisited in phase 3
rollout_plan: Week 1-2: engineering spike - storage schema for reserve windows and token ledger; autotune model selection and baseline calculations
Week 3-4: implement API + Console view; surface recommendations in staging; internal alpha with Platform team
Week 5: SRE chaos tests for burst preemption mapping and token exhaustion scenarios
Week 6: Security review and compliance checks; create on-call playbook
Week 7: Canary with 5 pilot tenants (opt-in) with manual accept flow
Week 8-10: collect telemetry, iterate on autotune thresholds, and expand to >50 tenants; prepare release notes and billing impact report
links: Related ticket ENG-22114: kernel scheduling change to reduce preemption latency
open_questions: What safety multiplier should the autotune engine default to for enterprise tenants vs startups?
Should reserve windows be billable as prorated minutes or only full-day increments?
What SLA/penalty model applies if autotune recommendations are applied and performance degrades?
Is it acceptable to persist token ledger entries in our existing time-series store or do we need a transactional backend?
notes: Stakeholder feedback from Jan 2025 working session emphasized visibility for burst decisions over full automation
Early experiments show short reserve windows (2-6 hours) reduce wasted-reserve by ~22% in synthetic traffic
We will coordinate billing changes with Finance before any automatic application of reserve changes
